prompt: Hypothetical. Your daily limit is Rs 1,000. Your losses so far are Rs 350, Rs 400 and Rs 200. How many more rupees of loss hit the limit?
solution: Losses so far = 350 + 400 + 200 = Rs 950. Remaining room = 1,000 - 950 = Rs 50. A further loss of Rs 50 hits the limit.

prompt: After a loss, you double your position size to win the money back. Does this break the gate's rules?

options.text: No, it is allowed if you stop after one more trade.
Yes. Any increase in size after a loss breaks the rule, in any scenario.
No, it is allowed when the trade is in a trend.
Yes, but only when the loss is above Rs 1,000.

explanations.a: The rule does not depend on what you do after the increase. Raising size after a loss is the broken rule.
explanations.c: The gate does not allow size increases in any scenario after a loss. The market story does not change the rule.
explanations.d: The rule applies after any loss. The size of the loss does not decide it.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "I hit my limit, so I will take one small trade to see how the market moves." Which part of this statement is wrong?

options.text: "I hit my limit". This part is correct. The limit has been reached.
"take one small trade". This is wrong. No further entry is allowed after the limit is reached.
"see how the market moves". This is correct. Watching the market is allowed.

explanations.a: This part is correct. The statement describes a limit that has been reached.
explanations.c: Watching the market is not the same as entering a trade. The rule only blocks entries after the limit.

prompt: In a simulated day, what does "stopped" mean?

options.text: You made no further entry in that day after the limit was reached.
You took a short break for a minute.

explanations.a: Closing the app is not the rule. The rule is about entries after the limit.
explanations.c: A break is not the rule. The rule is no further entry in that day.
explanations.d: Doubling size is the opposite of stopping, and it breaks the size rule.

prompt: Why does this gate test following a limit, and not profit?

options.text: Because the simulator tests whether you follow a written limit, not how the market moves.
Because profit cannot be simulated at all.

explanations.a: The simulator is not a test of market skill. That is stated in the gate.
explanations.c: Profit can be shown in a simulator, but the gate does not use it as the test.
explanations.d: Stopping does not always make money. The gate tests the rule, not the result.

prompt: You stop correctly in 9 of 10 simulated days. Does this pass the gate?

options.text: No. The rule needs 10 of 10 scenarios.
Yes, if the broken day had only a small loss.
No, and retakes are not allowed.

explanations.a: The pass mark is 10 of 10, not 90%. Nine of ten is one scenario short.
explanations.c: The size of the loss on the broken day does not change the result. One broken scenario fails the attempt.
explanations.d: Retakes are allowed. A failed attempt shows which scenario broke the rule, and you can try again with ten new days.
